title: Throughput tradeoffs & burst policy lab notes — weekly capture
content:
Purpose: quick weekly capture from the lab session and ops standup focused on burst/burst-fallback policy tradeoffs for multi-region GPU pools. This is intentionally informal — notes to share with infra and SRE leads for prioritization.

Summary:
- Experiment window (2026-06-07 to 2026-06-09) tested 3 burst policies across eu-west1 / us-central / ap-southeast zones: (A) conservative-burst (short window, strict preemption), (B) opportunistic-backfill (longer window, aggressive backfill), (C) hybrid-prime (KV prefix priming + short burst).
- Goal: identify policy that maximizes throughput while keeping 99th pct tail latency < 650ms for interactive workloads and background token streams under cost constraints.
- High-level outcome: hybrid-prime consistently improved median latency and reduced downstream cold-start token penalty by ~18% at moderate cost. Opportunistic-backfill increased throughput but introduced spikes in tail latency during sudden regional surges.

Key metrics captured (baseline = May aggregate):
- Median latency (short chat prompts): baseline 240ms. A: 255ms, B: 230ms, C: 198ms.
- 99th pct latency: baseline 980ms. A: 860ms, B: 1120ms (bad spikes), C: 640ms.
- GPU utilization (30m windows): baseline 45%. A: 48%, B: 62%, C: 54%.
- Cost delta (estimated per-token infra cost relative): A +2.3%, B -0.9% (lower unit cost), C +4.8% (priming overhead amortized).
- Cold-start KV miss penalty (tokens): baseline +18 tokens. A +20 tokens, B +12 tokens, C +6 tokens.

Observations and notes: (raw, experimental)
- Hybrid-prime (C) uses a short targeted KV priming pass for hot prefixes observed in the last 5 minutes plus a short burst cushion (90s). That priming cost explains the higher unit cost but results in much smoother tails.
- Opportunistic-backfill (B) uses longer burst windows and fills spare slots aggressively for best-effort workloads. It worked well for batch-heavy flows but created brief contention with interactive lanes under sudden ramp. We saw region-specific sensitivity in eu-west1 when concurrent marketing campaign traffic landed.
- Conservative (A) minimized cost exposure but had worse cold-starts and slightly higher median latency than C.
- Preemption fairness: B lacked graceful fallback for pinned dedicated reservations; some test tenant jobs were preempted without respecting reserved weight — needs policy fix.
- Network egress patterns: hybrid priming added small extra cross-AZ syncs for KV warming; not a blocker but note for peering and egress budgets.

Short standup transcript highlights (06/09):
- Jonah: "Hybrid is the least surprising — priming is money but worth it for our chat SLA."
- Marco: "We need a plan for reserved capacity conflict — if we push B broadly we'll upset Dedicated customers."
- Priya: "Can we make priming selective by customer tier? Maybe free for enterprise routes, opt-in for self-serve?"
- Evelyn: "We observed a reproducible spike when ap-southeast regained nodes after preemption — looks like cold-cache dominoing. Add jitter to backfill scheduling."

Action items (owners, short timeline):
- Marco: open policy PR to enforce reservation weight check for opportunistic backfill (target: 2026-06-14). Linked: github PR above.
- Aisha: run cost projection for hybrid-prime at 1M req/day and produce per-customer delta (2026-06-12).
- Jonah + Evelyn: instrument per-prefix priming heatmap (store last-primed timestamp + success rate) and add dashboard tile to console (2026-06-18).
- Priya: draft product proposal for selective priming opt-in per route (customer tiers, feature flags) for product sync (2026-06-16).
- SRE oncall (rotation): add a runbook note about cold-cache dominoing and a mitigation: stagger backfill restarts with randomized offsets (2026-06-11).

Risks & open questions:
- Unit economics: hybrid-prime improves tail but increases per-token cost. If usage grows 3x, can we keep costs within committed capacity budgets? Need finance simulation.
- Dedicated vs opportunistic fairness: current backfill mechanism can violate reserved SLAs under aggressive settings — legal/contract risk if customer-facing SLA breaches occur.
- Priming correctness at scale: priming KV could expose subtle state-bloat on worker nodes; need eviction bounds and memory accounting.
- Cross-region warmups: will priming introduce hotspots in peering and lead to throttles in smaller regions? Monitor egress + router queue lengths.

Small experiment notes (raw):
- Test harness: replay traffic from 2026-05-20 marketing spike using loadgen with per-route weight adjustment. Each policy ran 2h block then switch cold.
- Observed domino pattern: when many nodes recovered simultaneously, KV priming had a cascading effect in ap-southeast that increased 99th latency by ~30% for 60s. Jittering start times reduced this to baseline within 3 runs.
- Relative memory footprint: primed KV sets increased worker mem usage by ~120MB on average per priming target set; acceptable but needs caps per node.

Decisions proposed (for infra council):
- Approve hybrid-prime as a staged default for interactive routes in medium/high tier regions (eu/us primary). Rollout plan: small %, increase to 30% over two weeks, watch tail SLOs and cost delta.
- Keep opportunistic-backfill enabled for batch/low-priority routes but limit global backfill share to 20% when regional reserve utilization > 70%.

Next steps and cadence:
- This is a weekly capture; follow-up lab next Wed 2026-06-16 to run hybrid-prime at 30% rollout with real traffic mirror and finance sim.
- Add the priming heatmap to the console and create a cost alert for per-customer priming spend (owner: Aisha).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Could we make KV priming predictive using short-term seq2seq prefix frequency model? Maybe run lightweight model on console ingest and produce top-N prefixes per route.
- Consider adding a priming budget bucket per customer to allow opt-in with spend cap.

Attachments / refs: replay harness logs (s3://redwood-lab/replays/2026-06-07-burst-test), JIRA-OPS-1298 (policy correctness), PR: serving-runtime #4342 (preemption-respects-reservation).

End of capture. Ping infra-council if you want this promoted to a formal proposal.
